# Results — Study 760 (Michigan-Sentiment-Day)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Two believer claims about the
**University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment** release, tested on their own tapes: a
**release-day drift** on daily SPY, and a **level/regime** contrarian test — does
*low-then-rising* sentiment mark bottoms? Sentiment is a hardcoded, public monthly
snapshot of FRED `UMCSENT` (FRED's CSV endpoint is firewalled in this build); SPY is
yfinance daily adjusted close (total-return), used daily for the event study and month-end
sampled for the regime test. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sentiment tape | UMich Index of Consumer Sentiment (1966:Q1=100); **hardcoded monthly snapshot** of FRED `UMCSENT`, final print |
| Equity tape | yfinance daily **SPY** adjusted close (total-return adjusted); daily for the event study, month-end for the regime test |
| Release-date proxy | **second Friday** of each month (UMich preliminary-release day); a labelled schedule proxy, not the official calendar |
| Window | monthly frame 1993-01-31 → 2026-04-30 (**400** months; **33.2** years); daily SPY 1993-01 → 2026-06 (8,405 days) |
| Regime signal | **LOW** = sentiment ≤ trailing 30th percentile (expanding, ≥36-mo warmup, no look-ahead); **RISING** = level > level 3 months prior |
| Entry / costs | regime: enter at month-end after the mid-month print (**no extra lag**, print is already public); overlay: 1-month execution lag, 10 bps one-way per switch |

> **Snapshot caveat (named on the Signal axis).** FRED is firewalled here, so the sentiment
> series is a hardcoded monthly snapshot of the **final** `UMCSENT` print (Michigan also
> publishes a mid-month *preliminary* reading; the release-day study keys off the prelim
> schedule but the level is the settled monthly value). The famous troughs — 1980, 2008–09,
> Aug 2011, the **all-time-low 50.0 of June 2022**, and 2025 — are included faithfully. The
> release-date proxy (second Friday) shifts a day or two around holidays; that approximation
> is labelled, not hidden.

## A. Release-day drift — is the print a market mover?

The preliminary sentiment number prints mid-month (≈10:00 ET Friday). If it moved markets,
SPY would show a release-day reaction and, when the print carries a surprise
(surprise = sentiment*ₜ* − sentiment*ₜ₋₁*, a labelled proxy for beat-vs-consensus), a
tradable next-day **drift** in the surprise's direction (entered at the release-day close —
the print is already public, no look-ahead).

| event | n | mean SPY return | vs all-day mean | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| release day (close-to-close) | 401 | **+6.2 bp** | +4.8 bp | **+0.23** |

| next-day drift by surprise | n | mean | | Welch *t* (beat − miss) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| after a **beat** (sentiment up) | 196 | +8.2 bp | | — |
| after a **miss** (sentiment down) | 204 | +17.1 bp | | **−0.64** |
| (2-day drift) beat vs miss | 196 / 204 | +23.4 vs +43.7 bp | | **−1.31** |

The release day is **indistinguishable from an average day** (+6.2 bp vs +4.8 bp,
*t* = +0.23). Worse for the drift story, the post-release move runs the **wrong way**: the
market drifts *more* after a sentiment **miss** than after a beat (1-day *t* = −0.64, 2-day
*t* = −1.31). There is no announcement drift you could put on. **Release-day drift — NONE.**

## B. Level/regime — does low-then-rising sentiment mark bottoms?

Forward SPY returns in LOW months (sentiment ≤ trailing 30th percentile) and in the
believers' **LOW-and-RISING** bottom set, against the unconditional base rate. Welch *t*
compares each set's forward mean to the base. **`p_block`** is a circular block bootstrap
(12-month block) p — the honest, autocorrelation-aware significance, because overlapping
H-month returns make the naive Welch *t* over-reject.

| horizon | base mean | LOW mean | *t* (low) | **LOW&RISING mean** | n | Welch *t* | **block-boot *p*** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | +0.95%  | +1.02% | +0.19 | **+1.55%**  | 70 | +1.01 | 0.090 |
| 3-month  | +2.81%  | +2.85% | +0.05 | **+3.73%**  | 68 | +0.85 | 0.261 |
| 6-month  | +5.77%  | +5.41% | −0.33 | **+8.21%**  | 67 | +1.54 | 0.203 |
| 12-month | +11.97% | +11.55% | −0.25 | **+18.65%** | 64 | **+3.55** | **0.103** |

Two things jump out. (1) **The sentiment *level* alone carries nothing** — LOW months are a
dead ringer for the base rate at every horizon (*t* between +0.19 and −0.33). Cheap doesn't
mean it goes up. (2) The **LOW-and-RISING** set *does* beat the base badly at 12 months
(**+18.7% vs +12.0%**, naive *t* = **+3.55**) — which looks like a real bottom-timer. But
that 12-month return is a heavily **overlapping** object: the 64 signal months collapse into
just **21 independent episodes** (post-crash recoveries: 2003, 2009, 2020, 2022–23…), and a
block bootstrap that respects the overlap puts the p at **0.103** — it *can't clear the
bar*. The signal is real-as-lore, weak-as-edge: "buy after a sentiment low once it turns up"
is really "buy after a crash," recovered by a statistic that flatters small clustered
samples.

## Tradability — the "buy the bottom" overlay

Long SPY only in LOW-and-RISING months, else in cash (1-month execution lag; 10 bps one-way
per switch; Sharpe excess-of-zero, cash leg = 0, labelled; raced against buy-and-hold on the
total-return month-end tape).

| book | ann. mean | ann. Sharpe | switches | exposure |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| buy-and-hold SPY | **+11.3%** | **0.77** | — | 100% |
| overlay, gross | +3.3% | 0.46 | 53 | 18% |
| overlay, net @ 10 bps | **+3.1%** | **0.44** | 53 | 18% |

The overlay is **out of the market 82% of the time** (it only fires in the rare
bottoming set), so even though those months are genuinely above-average it earns just
**+3.1%/yr** — a third of buy-and-hold — at a *lower* Sharpe (0.44 vs 0.77). You cannot beat
buy-and-hold by being long a small, mostly-post-crash subset of months. **Tradability —
MIRAGE.** (The signal is a lean-*in* long tilt, not a market-timing overlay; the honest way
to "trade" it is to already own equities — which buy-and-hold does for free.)

## Robustness — the naive *t* is big everywhere, the bootstrap never clears

| variation (12-month LOW&RISING) | n | LOW&RISING mean | naive Welch *t* | **block-boot *p*** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| percentile ≤ 20% | 47 | +18.6% | +3.08 | 0.159 |
| percentile ≤ 30% (base) | 64 | +18.7% | **+3.55** | **0.103** |
| percentile ≤ 40% | 89 | +16.0% | +2.30 | 0.187 |
| momentum window **k = 1** | 75 | +15.1% | +1.51 | 0.274 |
| momentum window **k = 6** | 66 | +18.2% | +3.90 | 0.111 |
| **drop 2008–09** (ex-GFC) | 64 | +18.1% | +3.63 | 0.115 |
| **drop 2020** (ex-COVID) | 59 | +17.0% | +2.37 | 0.237 |

The pattern is the tell: the **naive *t* is 2.3–3.9 in every spec** — and the
autocorrelation-aware **block bootstrap p never drops below 0.10**. Dropping the GFC or COVID
barely moves the naive *t* (the effect isn't one crash) yet the bootstrap still won't certify
it — because the underlying object is ~20 clustered recoveries however you slice the window.
A signal that is "significant" only through the one statistic that ignores its clustering is
the textbook **WEAK**.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine (and the bootstrap) are faithful

A deterministic monthly sentiment + daily SPY-like series with a *planted* link: a
LOW-and-RISING month lifts the **next 12 months** of returns by a total of `edge`. The
detector *and the block bootstrap* must recover a real planted edge and must **not**
manufacture significance when the true edge is zero.

| planted edge (12-mo total) | n LOW&RISING | LOW&RISING 12m mean | base 12m mean | Welch *t* | **block-boot *p*** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no link) | 29 | +1.67% | +1.73% | **−0.02** | 0.332 |
| **+0.10** (large link) | 29 | +61.23% | +13.00% | **+8.35** | **0.004** |

With **no** planted link the test sits at *t* = −0.02, block-boot p = 0.33 (no false
positive). A large planted link drives *t* to +8.35 **and the block bootstrap to p = 0.004** —
proving the bootstrap isn't merely conservative: when the edge is genuinely there, it fires.
So the real-tape block-boot p ≈ 0.10 is a *true* "can't-certify," not a broken or
over-cautious test.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED** (`None` on the release-day drift · `Weak` on the level). The release-day
  reaction is a non-event (*t* = +0.23) and the surprise drift runs the *wrong* way (bigger
  after misses). The bottom-timer's naive 12-month *t* = +3.55 *looks* real but rests on ~21
  clustered post-crash recoveries; a 12-month block bootstrap can't clear it (*p* = 0.10),
  and the sentiment **level alone is flat** (*t* ≈ 0). Real-as-lore, weak-as-edge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "buy the bottom" overlay is in the market only 18% of the
  time and earns **+3.1%/yr** (Sharpe 0.44) vs buy-and-hold **+11.3%** (Sharpe 0.77). The
  signal is a lean-in long tilt you can't beat passive with.
- **Bottom-timer? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The one horizon where the naive statistic screams (12m,
  overlapping) is exactly where it's least trustworthy; the autocorrelation-aware bootstrap
  and the 21-episode count both say "a handful of recoveries," not a certifiable early tell.
